### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/package.json`, `packages/lint/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/package.json`, `packages/lint/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3f118220d9dd50e3566f0e8076cdec10129953ad` — the merge of head `481d40492ddfc7af48d6362f844571efc6f44d32` into base `a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3f118220d9dd50e3566f0e8076cdec10129953ad && git checkout 3f118220d9dd50e3566f0e8076cdec10129953ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53 481d40492ddfc7af48d6362f844571efc6f44d32 && git checkout -B drift-repro a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53 && git merge --no-ff 481d40492ddfc7af48d6362f844571efc6f44d32

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a5cb4f1bf03293ebbe8033ba4d813bf940575d53` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review — CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER · 2026-11-07T14:48Z

Head-sha: `775c97b55e9e5c06f3c29fc6c0c7d4e96a790637`

Scope: the whole non-prose diff (owed by `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, claim 6708318947), read against ADR-0146 D3 as amended by #31027 (Decided-here 10–12), rulings 6691022506 / 6691217245, pointer 6693814307, reports 6707849840 / 6708291325. Independent Fable review; the seat read its findings against the code.

**Verdict: PASS on conformance, with two should-fixes the seat requires before ACCEPT** (patch round on this PR).

Conforms (checked):
- Unit = App: `appOf` (`metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts:146-204`) is Decided-here 11 literally (App → itself; kernel → itself; declared Apps, else the walk through declared parents, cycle-safe; several → the namespace holder, else `undefined` → `pairOf` `no_single_app`). The ensure door answers the App's pair for any member; 422 only for an owner outside the App; kernel 409 judged first. Uninstall refusal reads the pair named for the package (`objectql/src/registry.ts:7394-7398`).
- The two new 409s are exactly Q11 (`no_single_app`) and Q12 (same-App legacy owner, guarded by `appOf(ownerBase) === appId`, so an outsider stays 422 — pinned).
- No escalation: `widenPairClosureToAppMembers` (`protocol-write-package-scope.ts:55-80`) widens only for a pair that declares its App, only over installed packages whose `pairOf` is this pair; never kernel, never uninstalled.
- Public surface and changeset: every changed/new `@objectstack/metadata-core` export is declared; `appOf(id, installed) ?? id` migration correct; declaration lines, BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` defensible under D8). Ablations consistent with the report.

Should-fix 1 — undeclared narrowing of a legacy pair (contradicts Q12 "honoured as today"):
- `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:761-779` `isPairRowRemoval` still asks the single `pairOf`, so a legacy member pair (`<module>.custom`) deleting its own declared override is no longer a pair-row removal (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:428`, `:781`: intent flips to `override-artifact` and it loses the pass past the sealed-removal refusal). Thread `isPairOf` as `judgeOverrideWrite` does (`:1170-1171`).
- Same family: `pairOfAddedMember` (`protocol-write-gates.ts:654-660`) and the extensions census in `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:3993` read only the App's pair. Make them read `pairsOf` / `isPairOf`, or, if a reader is deliberately App-pair-only, name it in the changeset's BREAKING list.

Should-fix 2 — pin Q12 end to end: one dispatcher-level test that a legacy `<module>.custom` override row is still served at the module's address (read by name, list and layered) and that the legacy pair can delete its own override, with an ablation (single `pairOf` back ⇒ red).

Nits (optional): a legacy pair of a module the newer App version no longer delivers resolves to itself and answers 422, not Q12's 409; the lint rule (`validate-customization-namespace.ts:123`) is silent for a no-single-App package; `@objectstack/lint`'s new `workspace:*` dependency on metadata-core is named in the PR body only.

Also on record: `PR-body guards` red on this head is the seat's own claim record (`check:closing-target-claim` read the original `Claim:`'s branch); a consolidated `Claim:` naming `claude/project-thread-oj61dz` is now on #29594, and the next push re-runs the guard.

## Contract review — delta round 2

Head-sha: `fb2fd21eb9d05368b49eb24320d1586b40dac847`

**Delta review · 2026-11-07T16:32Z**

Scope: the patch commits `c0172ddddc`, `f446e8a011`, `da5e499299` and `787f842cb7`. `fb2fd21eb9` is a clean merge of main (`git show --cc` is empty). This is an independent Fable review of the code that implements ADR-0146 Q12 (narrowed review rule of 2026-11-07). The seat checked its two should-fixes against the tree.

**Verdict: both round-1 should-fixes are resolved; two new should-fixes before ACCEPT.**

Resolved (checked):
- `isPairRowRemoval` now asks `isPairOf`, and the three call sites in `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` read it unchanged. `pairsOfAddedMember` / `findPairAddedMemberRow` read every pair in `pairsOf` order. The runtime extensions census iterates `pairsOf`, and `readBaseContributions` excludes all pairs.
- Every remaining single-`pairOf(` site was judged: the ensure door, fix landing, overlay migration, App-pair closure, import landing, and remedy and message text. Each says where a new customization lands, so each is App-pair by design. No reader that serves or lists customizations is App-pair-only, so the changeset's "No reader is App-pair-only" holds.
- Nothing is widened. A legacy id joins `pairsOf` only when `<base>.custom` is installed, a sibling module stays out, kernel keeps `[kernel.custom]`, and an outsider's `.custom` never enters. Precedence (App pair first, then legacy) is the same in by-name, list and layered reads.
- The new test runs real ObjectQL, SQL and protocol behind the real doors (`HttpDispatcher` reads, `RestServer` DELETE), with rows seeded straight into the store. The `doc` ablation goes red for the stated reason.

Should-fix A — changeset: `.changeset/29594-app-customization-pair.md` omits `@objectstack/runtime`. Yet `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` now changes the census and contributions that `GET /packages/:id/customizations` answers, and AGENTS.md requires a changeset entry for every published package changed. Add `'@objectstack/runtime'` to the frontmatter at the level AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives; it rides the same `feat`, and the header scope list should name it.

Should-fix B — test topology: `meta-legacy-pair-served.test.ts` builds the protocol with no `environmentId`. So the `environmentId !== undefined` block in `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` (~:449–510), which holds `refusePackagedBaseRemoval` and its `!pairRowRemoval` guard (~:502), is never entered. The ablation is red only through the repository's `intent` gate. A regression that drops `!pairRowRemoval` from that guard would stay green. Give the removal case an `environmentId` (or run it under both topologies), and add one ablation: drop `!pairRowRemoval` at the guard ⇒ red.

Nits (optional): nothing pins the legacy branch of `pairsOfAddedMember` (a bundle member a legacy pair added) or the census reading a legacy pair's extensions, though the changeset asserts both. `packages.ts` ~:3997 puts `if (…) for (…) {` on one line.

After the patch, the seat does an in-seat delta review (the changeset and test topology implement no contract text). Then ACCEPT and landing: Size gate, then human merge.

## Contract review — ACCEPT

Head-sha: `481d40492ddfc7af48d6362f844571efc6f44d32`

**ACCEPT · in-seat delta review · 2026-11-07T17:20Z**

Delta since round 2 (`fb2fd21eb9`): `b1ea4bc763` and `ef5fdb4439`, plus a clean merge of main. This review is in-seat: the changes are to the changeset and the test topology, which implement no contract text (narrowed review rule of 2026-11-07).

- Should-fix A is fixed. `.changeset/29594-app-customization-pair.md` names `'@objectstack/runtime': minor`, and the header scope list and the PR title name runtime.
- Should-fix B is fixed. Every case in `meta-legacy-pair-served.test.ts` runs under both topologies (host-config, and `environmentId: 'env_hotcrm'`), 6/6 green. The new ablation drops `!pairRowRemoval` from the guard in `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` and turns the environment-kernel `doc` removal red with `refusePackagedBaseRemoval`'s own "sealed against removal" refusal (1 failed / 5 passed). The host-config topology stays green, which is expected. Restored, 6/6 green. The earlier single-`pairOf` ablation (6709801932) still stands; that code has not changed since.
- The `packages.ts` one-line `if … for` nit is split. The two optional pins are not added, which is accepted.
- Readings: derived gates 111/111 exit 0 with `--ran` reconciled; the full dogfood battery passes on `481d40492d` (435 files / 3609 cases, VERDICT command-exit 0); CI is green on this head, with one job still running.
- Correction to round 2's last line: this PR is 1349 lines and touches no Tier H path, so no size gate and no human merge apply. The seat lands it through the merge queue.

All three review rounds are closed: the full Fable review at `775c97b55e`, Fable delta round 2 at `fb2fd21eb9`, and this one. Landing: ready, then auto-merge.
